extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers, ML practitioners, and developers of LLM-generated-text detection/forensic tools
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating tools that detect whether text was generated by large language models and (when possible) attribute the source to a specific LLM. Emphasis on methods that are model-specific, efficient, secure, and extendable to new models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-specific detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Detection should be model-specific and able to source text from specific LLMs (e.g., GPT-2, OPT, LLaMA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLMDet is described as 'model-specific' — detection should not only separate human vs machine but attribute text to particular LLMs. The paper demonstrates sourcing among named models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine-grained tracing / source attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Capability to perform fine-grained tracing to identify the originating model rather than merely classifying text as machine-generated vs human-authored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors contrast existing tools that 'can only differentiate between machine-generated and human-authored text' and emphasize the requirement for 'fine-grained tracing' to determine the specific source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediary judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for intermediary judgment (an intermediate/nuanced determination rather than only binary labels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract lists 'intermediary judgment' as a requirement that existing tools fail to meet; detection systems should provide more than a binary decision, enabling nuanced or intermediate assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid detection / efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The tool must enable rapid detection, with practical runtime performance for real-world use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLMDet claims to be 'x5.0 faster for recognizing human-authored text.' Evaluation should measure speed and benchmark detection latency against alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security (third-party operation without exposing models)
rubrics_metrics.description: The detection tool should be secure and operable by third parties (implying it need not require access to the candidate LLMs themselves).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper frames LLMDet as a 'third party' and 'secure' tool, contrasting with existing detectors that 'typically rely on access to LLMs.' Designs should avoid needing direct model access or exposing sensitive model internals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extendability to new models
rubrics_metrics.description: Ease of extending detection capabilities to newly released or open-source models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors state LLMDet 'can effortlessly extend its detection capabilities to a new open-source model.' Architectures should support adding models with minimal overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of salient n-gram next-token probabilities as features
rubrics_metrics.description: Record next-token probabilities of salient n-grams and use them as features to characterize text with respect to each LLM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLMDet 'records the next-token probabilities of salient n-grams as features' — implementers should extract and store such n-gram-level next-token probabilities for downstream scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxy perplexity per LLM
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a proxy perplexity for each candidate LLM using recorded features (e.g., salient n-gram next-token probabilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method calculates 'proxy perplexity for each LLM' from the salient n-gram probabilities; proxy perplexity serves as a per-model score to compare against observed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint analysis of proxy perplexities for attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the source model by jointly analyzing proxy perplexities across multiple LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLMDet 'jointly analys[es] the proxy perplexities of LLMs' to decide the source; attribution should be based on comparative/probabilistic assessment across model-specific perplexities rather than isolated thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: High precision in detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Detection should achieve high precision (minimizing false positives), as demonstrated by reported metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper reports '98.54% precision' in experiments — evaluations should include precision (and other relevant metrics) and aim for similarly high precision in production settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical performance evaluation and comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide experimental evidence showing detection performance, speed, and other claimed benefits, and compare against existing tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract emphasizes experimental results showing 'impressive detection performance while ensuring speed and security' and speedups; authors should report quantitative benchmarks (precision, runtime) and comparisons to prior methods.
